payload.say: Every animal has to find food. A goat eats grass, a tiger eats the goat. But a plant never goes anywhere. So where does a plant get its food from? It makes its own.

payload.say: A leaf needs three things. Sunlight from above, water pulled up from the roots, and a gas from the air called carbon dioxide. Put those three together and the leaf can build food.

payload.say: Inside every leaf there is a green colour called chlorophyll. That green is what catches the sunlight. No chlorophyll, no catching sunlight, no food. That is why almost every leaf you have ever seen is green.

Cellulose is a long chain of sugar molecules that gives plants their structure.  
It is the main part of the walls of leaf cells, like the frame of a house.  
We can see cellulose in things like cotton, paper, and wood, but we cannot eat it.
